events.headline: New York Declares Statewide Disaster Emergency Over Measles Outbreak
events.summary: Governor Hochul declared a State Disaster Emergency on October 5, 2026, effective through November 4, as New York reported 108 confirmed measles cases amid a broader US resurgence that has reached roughly 3,887 cases nationally, the worst since 1991. The order expands who can administer the measles vaccine and order testing, including pharmacists and paramedics.

events.headline: DR Congo Ebola Death Toll Rises to 4,080 as Transit Centre Burns Down
events.summary: The Ebola death toll in the Democratic Republic of Congo has reached 4,080 with 8,442 confirmed cases, the country's worst outbreak on record. A transit centre for infected patients at the Kigonze camp near Bunia, Ituri province, was burned down by soldiers searching for weapons, forcing roughly 19,000 displaced people to flee and setting back containment efforts amid worker exhaustion.

events.headline: Houthi Strikes Expand to Jazan and Najran Airports, Wounding Three in Saudi Arabia
events.summary: Houthi forces struck Jazan and Najran airports in Saudi Arabia, wounding three people, in an expansion of their drone-and-missile campaign beyond earlier strikes on Riyadh, Abha and Aden. The attacks mark a widening of Houthi targeting of Saudi civil aviation infrastructure.

events.headline: Russian Glide-Bomb Strike on Buses Kills at Least 30 in Kramatorsk, Deadliest in Week-Long Strike Campaign
events.summary: A Russian glide-bomb strike hit two passenger buses in Kramatorsk, Ukraine, killing at least 30 civilians in the deadliest single incident of a week-long Russian infrastructure bombing campaign that has also damaged bridges and killed six in Kyiv. A war-crimes investigation has been opened into the Kramatorsk attack.

events.headline: Eritrean Troops Cross Into Northern Ethiopia Near Adigrat, Raising Risk of State-to-State War
events.summary: Eritrean troops crossed into northern Ethiopia's Tigray region near Adigrat, prompting Ethiopia to demand an immediate withdrawal as the Tigray conflict's regionalization deepens. The incursion follows Eritrea's earlier severing of ties with Addis Ababa and raises the risk of direct state-to-state war.

events.headline: UN Report Names Political, Economic Figures Backing Haiti's Gangs Ahead of First Elections in a Decade
events.summary: A new United Nations report identified specific political and economic figures accused of financing and protecting Haiti's armed gangs, as the country prepares for its first elections in a decade amid continued gang expansion. The findings add pressure on authorities already struggling to contain escalating violence in Port-au-Prince.

events.headline: Saudi Coalition Destroys 82 Houthi Targets as Saudi Arabia, Turkey, Pakistan Activate Mecca Defense Pact
events.summary: The Saudi-led coalition said it destroyed 82 Houthi targets in "Operation Dawn of Yemen," while Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Pakistan activated the Mecca Joint Defence Agreement, a new multinational military pact. The moves mark a major escalation and expansion of the military alliance confronting Houthi forces in Yemen.

events.headline: US Charges Venezuela's Maduro and Wife Cilia Flores With Conspiracy to Commit Torture
events.summary: US federal prosecutors in Manhattan unsealed charges against Venezuelan President Nicolás Maduro and his wife Cilia Flores accusing them of conspiracy to commit torture against political opponents. The indictment marks a major escalation in Washington's legal campaign against the Maduro government.

events.headline: Kenya Confirms First Ebola Case and Death as Outbreak Reaches Nairobi
events.summary: Kenya confirmed its first Ebola case and death in Nairobi, involving a patient who had traveled from the Democratic Republic of Congo, marking the outbreak's spread to a major East African transit hub and its fourth affected country. Health authorities have launched contact tracing and containment measures in the capital.

events.headline: Pakistan Launches New Airstrikes on Afghanistan as Border Conflict Enters Third Week
events.summary: Pakistani airstrikes hit Kunar and Helmand provinces in Afghanistan on October 1, with Kabul and the UN mission in Afghanistan saying at least 9-10 civilians, including children, were killed. Pakistan said the strikes targeted TTP and Baloch separatist hideouts, killing 22 fighters, as hostilities continue into a third week following a September 18 suicide bombing in Pakistan.

events.headline: FlyDubai Co-Pilot Identified as Omani National in Cockpit Axe Attack
events.summary: An Omani co-pilot, reportedly identified as Hamam al-Hammami, attacked the captain with a crash axe aboard a flydubai flight from Dubai to Tel Aviv on October 1, 2026, wounding him. The aircraft, carrying 174 passengers, briefly plunged about 17,000 feet before passengers and crew subdued the attacker, and it made an emergency landing in Tabuk, Saudi Arabia. UAE officials called it an attempted terrorist act; the co-pilot had reportedly been barred from flying in Oman over extremist views.

events.headline: Hurricane Isaias Makes Landfall as Category 2 Storm on US Gulf Coast
events.summary: Hurricane Isaias made landfall near the Alabama-Florida border as a Category 2 storm on October 8-9, prompting multi-state emergency declarations and evacuations along the Gulf Coast. Authorities warned of storm surge, flooding and wind damage across coastal Alabama and the Florida Panhandle.

events.headline: Brazil Campaign Resumes With Flávio Bolsonaro Holding Narrow Lead Over Lula Ahead of Oct 25 Runoff
events.summary: Free campaign airtime resumed in Brazil's presidential race, with polls showing Flávio Bolsonaro holding a narrow lead over Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva ahead of the October 25 runoff. Both candidates are preparing for a scheduled October 11 debate as the race remains tight.

events.headline: Colombia's Petro Calls for Criminal Investigation of Trump Over Deadly US Boat Strikes
events.summary: Colombian President Gustavo Petro called for a criminal investigation into US President Trump over deadly US military strikes on suspected drug-smuggling boats in the Caribbean and eastern Pacific. The demand marks a sharp diplomatic escalation between Bogotá and Washington over the ongoing strike campaign.

events.headline: EU and China Hold Crunch Trade Talks in Beijing to Avert Trade War
events.summary: European Union and Chinese officials held high-stakes trade talks in Beijing aimed at averting an escalating trade war between the two blocs. The negotiations cover tariffs and market-access disputes that have strained EU-China economic relations.

events.headline: Singapore's Air Quality Hits Record-Worst PSI of 181 as Indonesian Haze Crisis Deepens
events.summary: Singapore's PSI index hit a 2026 record of 181 in its central region as transboundary haze from Indonesian wildfires worsened, prompting school closures in Johor, Malaysia. The record pollution level marks a significant escalation of the regional haze crisis.

events.headline: Brent Crude Rises to $104-105 a Barrel Amid Record Wave of Tanker Attacks in Strait of Hormuz
events.summary: Brent crude prices rose to around $104-105 a barrel after a record wave of tanker attacks in the Strait of Hormuz heightened fears of supply disruption. The market reaction reflects growing concern over escalating regional tensions affecting a critical global oil chokepoint.

events.headline: Hurricane Simón Strengthens Toward Major Hurricane Status Off Mexico's Pacific Coast
events.summary: Hurricane Simón intensified off Mexico's Pacific coast and was forecast to strengthen into a potential Category 4 storm between October 7-12, threatening Michoacán, Colima and Sinaloa. Mexican authorities issued coastal warnings and began evacuation preparations ahead of expected landfall.

events.headline: Peru's Congress Grants President Fujimori 90-Day Decree Powers on Security and El Niño
events.summary: Peru's Chamber of Deputies approved special decree powers for President Fujimori for 90 days to address security and anticipated El Niño-related flooding. The measure allows the executive to bypass normal legislative procedure on these issues.

events.headline: Suspected Boko Haram Militants Kill 15 Farmers in Marte, Borno State, Nigeria
events.summary: Suspected Boko Haram militants killed 15 farmers in an attack near Marte, Borno State, in northeastern Nigeria. The attack underscores the persistent insurgent threat to agricultural communities in the region.

events.headline: Anti-Migrant Violence Erupts in Soweto and Durban, South Africa
events.summary: Violence targeting foreign nationals broke out in Soweto, near Johannesburg, and in Durban, South Africa, on October 8. The unrest reflects recurring xenophobic tensions that have periodically flared in South African townships and cities.

events.headline: Ukraine Strikes Russia's Largest Oil Refinery in Omsk, 2,500km From the Border
events.summary: Ukrainian forces struck Russia's largest oil refinery in Omsk, roughly 2,500 kilometers from the Ukrainian border, in one of the deepest strikes of the war. The attack underscores Ukraine's expanding long-range strike capability against Russian energy infrastructure.

events.headline: France and Germany Strike Deal to Weaken EU's 2035 Combustion-Engine Car Phaseout
events.summary: France and Germany reached an agreement to further weaken the European Union's planned 2035 phaseout of internal combustion engine vehicles. The deal signals a significant shift in EU climate and automotive policy ahead of further negotiations.

events.headline: Myanmar Junta Airstrikes Kill at Least 10 at Gold-Mining Site in Sagaing Region
events.summary: Myanmar's military carried out airstrikes on a gold-mining site near the Thahpanseik Reservoir in Sagaing Region, killing at least 10 people. The strike is part of the junta's continuing air campaign against areas contested by resistance forces.

events.headline: Floods and Landslides Kill at Least 34 in Southern Myanmar's Dawei Region
events.summary: Floods and landslides killed at least 34 people, with some reports putting the toll as high as 41, in Dawei and Launglon townships in Myanmar's Tanintharyi Region. Around 20 people remained missing as rescue operations continued.

events.headline: China's Trade Surplus Widens to Record Pace Driven by AI-Fueled Export Surge
events.summary: China's trade surplus widened to a record pace in August, reaching $119.09 billion, driven by a 25% year-on-year export surge linked to AI infrastructure demand. The widening gap with the US, now the largest since January 2025, is reigniting trade tension concerns as markets reopened in early October.

events.headline: PAHO Member States Adopt New 2026-2035 Regional Strategy to Combat Dengue and Arboviral Diseases
events.summary: Member states of the Pan American Health Organization adopted a new ten-year regional strategy to combat dengue and other mosquito-borne arboviral diseases across the Americas. The plan comes amid rising case counts region-wide.

events.headline: Kosovo Lawmakers Elect Justina Shiroka Pula President, Averting Snap Election
events.summary: Kosovo's parliament elected Justina Shiroka Pula as president in a late-night vote, resolving the political deadlock that had triggered clashes between police and protesters earlier in the month. The vote averted a snap election that had loomed over the stalled push to curb the Hague war-crimes court.

events.headline: Russia Denies Second Plague Case in Siberia as WHO Presses for Formal Response
events.summary: Russian authorities dismissed reports of a second plague case linked to a Siberian laboratory as false information, after an earlier suspected plague death triggered a quarantine in Irkutsk. The World Health Organization is pressing Moscow for a formal, transparent response.

events.headline: Flash Floods Injure Six, Sweep Away Cars in Wealthy Santiago Suburb of Las Condes
events.summary: Flash floods struck the affluent Las Condes district of Santiago, Chile, injuring six people and sweeping away vehicles on October 8-9. The storm highlighted unusual severe-weather risk in the capital's normally dry foothill neighborhoods.

events.headline: Dozens Detained in Moscow as Communist Party Rally Turns Into Anti-Government Protest
events.summary: Moscow police detained dozens of people after a sanctioned Communist Party rally turned into a broader anti-government protest. The incident reflects rare public dissent inside Russia amid wartime economic pressures.

events.headline: Henri Kagan and Kenso Soai Win 2026 Nobel Prize in Chemistry for Chirality Research
events.summary: Henri Kagan and Kenso Soai were awarded the 2026 Nobel Prize in Chemistry for their research on chirality and asymmetric synthesis. The announcement was made in Stockholm and recognizes decades of foundational work in molecular chemistry.

events.headline: Dozens of Detainees Launch Hunger Strike at Folkston ICE Processing Center in Georgia
events.summary: Dozens of immigration detainees began a hunger strike at the Folkston ICE Processing Center in Georgia to protest conditions and detention policies. Advocacy groups say the action reflects wider unrest inside US immigration detention facilities.

events.headline: Pro-Russian Hacker Group Targets Italian Foreign Ministry Website With DDoS Attack
events.summary: The pro-Russian hacker group NoName057(16) launched a distributed denial-of-service attack against the website of Italy's Foreign Ministry. The incident is part of a broader pattern of pro-Russian cyberattacks against European government institutions.

events.headline: Russia Slashes Cancer-Care Funding Nearly Twelvefold as 2027 Defense Spending Hits Post-Soviet Record
events.summary: Russia's federal budget plan shows cancer-care funding cut by nearly twelvefold even as 2027 defense spending is set to reach a post-Soviet-era record. The allocation underscores the economic strain and shifting priorities created by Russia's prolonged war in Ukraine.

events.headline: Chile's Kast Withdraws Constitutional Security Reform After Cross-Party Rejection
events.summary: Chilean presidential figure José Antonio Kast withdrew a proposed constitutional security reform after it faced rejection from across the political spectrum. The move is a setback for Kast's security-focused platform ahead of upcoming political contests.

events.headline: Death of Eviction Symbol 'Maricarmen' Sparks Vigils and Protests Across Madrid
events.summary: The death of an elderly woman known as "Maricarmen," who had become a symbol of Spain's eviction and housing crisis, sparked vigils and protests across Madrid. The case has intensified public anger that earlier contributed to Prime Minister Sánchez's call for a snap election over housing policy.

events.headline: Former Israeli Military Chief Eisenkot Calls for Criminal Probe Into Netanyahu Over Oct 7 Record-Tampering
events.summary: Former Israeli military chief Gadi Eisenkot called for a criminal investigation into Prime Minister Netanyahu over allegations of tampering with official records related to the October 7 attacks. The call adds to mounting domestic political pressure on Netanyahu's government.

events.headline: Indonesian Civil Society Groups Sue Government for 'Gross Negligence' Over Wildfires
events.summary: Civil society groups filed a lawsuit accusing the Indonesian government of "gross negligence" in handling wildfires in Kalimantan and Sumatra that have fueled the regional haze crisis. A court hearing was held and adjourned to October 21.

events.headline: Red Alerts and Flash Floods Batter Barcelona and Girona as Storms Hit Catalonia
events.summary: Severe storms triggered red alerts and flash flooding across Barcelona and Girona in Catalonia, Spain, between October 3-6, killing two people. The flooding is part of a broader pattern of extreme autumn rainfall affecting multiple regions of Spain.

events.headline: Deloitte Canada Cuts 2027 Growth Forecast to 1.6% Amid Deepening US Tariff War
events.summary: Deloitte Canada lowered its 2027 economic growth forecast to 1.6%, citing escalating effects of the ongoing US-Canada tariff dispute. The downgrade signals growing concern about the trade war's drag on the Canadian economy.

events.headline: Arafura Rare Earths Breaks Ground on A$1.8 Billion Nolans Project Near Alice Springs
events.summary: Arafura Rare Earths broke ground on its A$1.8 billion Nolans rare-earths project north of Alice Springs, Australia, backed by the Australian government, Hancock Prospecting, Hyundai-Kia and Siemens Gamesa. The project is positioned as a strategic move to diversify global rare-earth supply chains away from China.

events.headline: Azerbaijani Serviceman Crosses Into Armenia, Shoots and Wounds Woman in Syunik
events.summary: An Azerbaijani serviceman crossed the border into Armenia's Syunik province and shot and wounded a woman near Shaki village. The incident adds new friction to the fragile Armenia-Azerbaijan peace process.

events.headline: European Commission Unveils EU Enlargement Reform Package Ahead of October Summit
events.summary: The European Commission unveiled a package of enlargement reforms ahead of the October 15-16 EU summit, aimed at streamlining the accession process for candidate countries. The package comes amid ongoing debate over the pace of Balkan and Eastern European EU integration.

events.headline: DRC Military Court Sentences 27 Soldiers to Death for Cowardice Near Uvira
events.summary: A Democratic Republic of Congo military court sentenced 27 soldiers to death for cowardice following a trial linked to battlefield setbacks near Uvira in South Kivu. The verdict reflects the army's efforts to enforce discipline amid continuing conflict with armed groups in the east.

events.headline: Thai Opposition Files Censure Motion Against PM Anutin Over 'Blue Regime' Corruption Allegations
events.summary: Thailand's opposition filed a censure motion against Prime Minister Anutin and 17 other ministers over alleged corruption linked to the so-called "Blue Regime." The motion sets up a parliamentary no-confidence debate over the government's conduct.

events.headline: Singapore National Serviceman Dies After Collapsing During Basic Military Training
events.summary: A Singapore national serviceman died after collapsing during Basic Military Training on Pulau Tekong. The Ministry of Defence said it is investigating the circumstances of his death.

events.headline: M4.9 Earthquake in Afghanistan's Hindu Kush Felt Across Kashmir and Northern Pakistan
events.summary: A magnitude 4.9 earthquake struck deep beneath Afghanistan's Hindu Kush region near Fayzabad, with tremors felt across Kashmir and northern Pakistan. No damage or casualties were reported.
